subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should this issue be resolved by making live Gateway memory runtime health the status source of truth, or is the current `not checked` mitigation enough for `openclaw status`?
rationale: Current main only softens the misleading wording and still has local plugin probing for memory-reporting status paths; choosing the permanent status contract affects plugin authors and operator diagnostics.

options.title: Adopt live-Gateway status contract
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept current mitigation
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for normal/deep status, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue with the current release behavior as the product decision.

options.title: Revive the narrow fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove human plus JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

recommendation.title: Adopt live-Gateway status contract
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The central status/memory runtime history points most strongly to steipete for deciding the product boundary and owner placement.
